messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Media and Language and linguistics in Belgium, Germany, Spain, Greece, France, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Finland, Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Latvia, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Sweden, United Kingdom, and Lithuania during the 2010s?
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: Eurobarometer media use survey 2010 2019 dataset GESIS
European Social Survey media use language variables data 2010 2018 countries
Eurobarometer Europeans and their languages 2012 dataset GESIS
Eurostat language skills foreign languages adult education survey 2016 dataset
action.query: Eurobarometer media use survey 2010 2019 dataset GESIS

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Flash Eurobarometer 313: User Language Preferences Online (2011)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.10730","justification":"Excellent match for both Media and Language and Linguistics. Conducted in January–February 2011, this dataset examines respondents' mother tongues, languages used to read and watch online content, languages used for online communication, and preferences for accessing websites in different languages. Its geographic coverage includes all 28 countries requested, including the United Kingdom. Available through the GESIS Data Archive as study ZA5473."},{"title":"Eurobarometer Media Use Trend Data (2010–2019)","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/eurobarometer-data-service/overview/eb-trends-trend-files/list-of-trends/media-use","justification":"Highly relevant longitudinal data covering media consumption across European countries during the entire 2010s. Includes television viewing, radio listening, newspaper readership, internet use, and online social networking. The GESIS documentation identifies annual Eurobarometer waves from 2010 through 2019, enabling comparative research into media habits across the requested European countries. Particularly useful for investigating national differences in media consumption and communication."},{"title":"European Social Survey, Round 5 (2010)","url_or_doi":"https://microdata.worldbank.org/index.php/catalog/2932","justification":"Cross-national survey dataset collected in 2010–2011, containing information about media exposure, internet use, social attitudes, and demographic characteristics. Relevant variables include television consumption, radio listening, newspaper readership, and personal internet use. Supports comparative research into media behavior and its relationship with social and cultural characteristics. Covers a subset of the requested European countries rather than all 28."},{"title":"Eurostat Adult Education Survey: Number of Foreign Languages Known (2011 and 2016)","url_or_doi":"https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/edat_aes_l21/default/table?lang=en","justification":"European statistical dataset measuring adults' self-reported knowledge of foreign languages. Includes observations from the 2011 and 2016 Adult Education Surveys, allowing comparisons of multilingualism during the 2010s. The 2016 survey provides statistics for the EU-28, including the United Kingdom. Particularly relevant to language proficiency, multilingualism, linguistic diversity, and cross-national differences in language knowledge."},{"title":"Eurostat: Pupils by Education Level and Modern Foreign Language Studied","url_or_doi":"https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/educ_uoe_lang01/default/table?lang=en","justification":"Harmonized European education statistics measuring foreign-language learning by education level and language studied. Includes observations from the 2010s and supports comparisons between European countries, including the requested EU member states and the United Kingdom where historical data are available. Useful for investigating foreign-language education, linguistic diversity, and the development of multilingual capabilities."},{"title":"Eurostat: Individuals Using the Internet for Participating in Social Networks","url_or_doi":"https://dgs-p.eige.europa.eu/data/view?code=ta_resdig_dig_intuse__isoc_bde15cua__socnet&orderby=2019&orderdir=dsc","justification":"European statistical data on individuals using the internet to participate in social networks. Includes observations from the 2010s, with country-level comparisons and demographic breakdowns. Relevant to digital media, online communication, and internet-mediated social interaction. The historical EU-28 series is particularly useful for comparing social networking behavior across the requested countries, including the United Kingdom."},{"title":"European Social Survey: Cross-National Survey Data, 2010–2018","url_or_doi":"https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/data/","justification":"Official data portal for the European Social Survey, providing access to multiple survey rounds conducted during the 2010s, including 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, and 2018. Relevant topics include media use, internet access, social trust, national identity, and demographic characteristics. The surveys support analysis of communication behavior and cultural differences across participating European countries. Country participation varies by round, so the complete requested country list is not covered in every wave."},{"title":"GESIS Eurobarometer Data Service: Survey Data and Documentation (2010–2019)","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/eurobarometer-data-service/data-and-documentation","justification":"Official research-data access point for Eurobarometer surveys, including Standard, Special, and Flash Eurobarometer datasets collected during the 2010s. Relevant topics include media consumption, online communication, language preferences, multilingualism, and foreign-language proficiency. Many surveys cover all 28 requested countries, including the United Kingdom. Provides access to survey datasets, questionnaires, codebooks, and methodological documentation, making it valuable for identifying additional studies at the intersection of media and linguistics."}]}
